name: Scroll to text fragment
plain: Highlights and scrolls to quoted text in a page when a link includes #:~:text=.
meaning: A link can point at one sentence on any page. The browser, not the page, does the highlighting, and the page cannot see the fragment, so it cannot learn what the visitor was searching for.

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Only full navigations in top-level browsing contexts
steps: Person opens a link with a text directive
Browser finds the first match and scrolls
Highlight is drawn by the browser

limits.headline: Can scroll to and highlight text on a page when you open a special link
limits.user_action: You tap a link that ends with a text highlight, like a link shared from search results.
can: Jump to quoted text on the page and highlight it
Open from a link that someone shared with you
Show a short highlight in yellow
cannot: Let the page's own code see which text was highlighted
Highlight text that is not on the page
Highlight text inside embedded frames in most cases
Run without you opening that link

story.what_it_is: A link can highlight and scroll to exact words on a page.

marketing.name: Text fragments
marketing.pitch: Chrome's docs say you can link right to a specific passage of a page.

story.for_you: You tap a link and the page jumps to a highlighted sentence. Search results use it so you land on the answer, not the top of the page.
story.for_makers: Makers and search engines use it to send people to the exact passage. Google search snippets use it and some sharing tools make quote links with it.

use_cases.example: A search result links to the exact sentence that answers your question.
A reader copies a link to a quote from an article and sends it to a friend.
A teacher links students to the exact definition inside a long page.
A research tool saves quotes as links back to the highlighted text.
A site may use it to find out whether specific words exist on a page.
A docs site links straight to the line about a function.

technical_bounds: Needs user activation or browser-initiated navigation (search results, address bar)
Page script cannot read the directive (stripped from location.hash and document.fragmentDirective is empty)
Matches visible text only, word boundary aware, first match wins
Cross-origin initiated navigations need noopener; not applied in iframes
Can be disabled by Document-Policy: force-load-at-top

abuse: Probing page contents with crafted links (mitigated by activation, no readable fragment)
